title: Split-and-Scale Latent 3D Representations
excerpt: Latent 3D representations have significantly expanded the capabilities of modern shape modeling, enabling compact encoding of 3D scenes and supporting powerful 3D generative models. Despite this progress, current representations struggle to capture the fine details of complex objects, fundamentally limited by the capacity of their latents. However, scaling latent capacity at training time is computationally expensive and often infeasible under memory limits, and naively increasing the number of latents at inference fails to make effective use of the added capacity. In this paper, we address…

ai.summary: Apple ML introduces a split‑and‑scale latent 3D representation that partitions the latent space to increase capacity while keeping training memory manageable, enabling finer detail capture in 3D generative models.
ai.why: Developers building 3D generative systems can adopt the method to train higher‑fidelity models without prohibitive GPU memory.

title: Evidence-Governed Adoption of Self-Generated Updates in Autonomous AI Agents
excerpt: Autonomous agents modify prompts, memories, tools, workflows, and policies using interaction histories. Yet a plausible modification is not necessarily suitable for persistent adoption: candidate selection is adaptive, evaluators may be imperfect, and local gains can hide degradation against an earlier baseline. We introduce Evidence-Governed Evolution (EGE), a framework for governing adoption of self-generated agent modifications. EGE separates candidate generation from confirmatory adoption, evaluates frozen candidates on fresh paired audits, requires meaningful improvement on a prespecified primary objective, protects declared capabilities through reference-relative non-inferiority…

ai.summary: The paper proposes Evidence-Governed Evolution (EGE), a framework that separates generation of self‑modifications for autonomous AI agents from a confirmatory adoption step, using evidence from interaction histories to decide which changes to persist.
ai.why: It offers a systematic way to improve agent reliability, helping developers build agents that can safely update their prompts, tools, or policies over time.

title: JFinBench: A Continuously Refreshable Japanese Financial Benchmark from the Latest Certification Exams
excerpt: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to finance, creating a need for benchmarks that evaluate their capabilities across financial systems with different regulations and practices. However, existing financial benchmarks provide limited coverage of country-specific financial systems, and they are difficult to keep up to date as released questions leak into training data. We introduce JFinBench, a Japanese financial benchmark comprising 321 examples from the 2026 editions of six regularly administered certification exams covering accounting, tax, financial planning, and banking. To construct it, we develop a human-in-the-loop agentic pipeline in which a coding agent writes…

ai.summary: JFinBench is a new Japanese financial benchmark containing 321 questions drawn from the 2026 editions of six certification exams, designed to be continuously refreshed to stay current with regulatory changes.
ai.why: Provides a localized, up‑to‑date test set for evaluating LLM performance on Japan‑specific finance tasks, useful for developers building financial AI products in that market.

title: eDMD: Endpoint Distribution Matching for Few-Step Diffusion Distillation
excerpt: Distribution matching distillation (DMD) has emerged as a leading paradigm for distilling diffusion models into few-step students, where an auxiliary fake score model tracks the student's distribution and the discrepancy between the teacher and fake predictions drives the student toward the teacher. In multi-step distillation, although only the student's final output is delivered, existing methods train the fake model on intermediate states or across all denoising steps. Consequently, the student's update signal becomes entangled with intermediate distributions, which can distort the matching direction and remain nonzero even after the student's final outputs already match the teacher…

ai.summary: eDMD presents Endpoint Distribution Matching, a method that trains a fake score model only on the student’s final output to guide few‑step diffusion distillation, improving efficiency over existing multi‑step approaches.
ai.why: It can reduce the number of diffusion steps needed for high‑quality generation, benefiting developers building lightweight generative models.

title: MIRIX-2.0: Multi-Agent Memory System
excerpt: Long-term memory lets LLM agents personalize, stay consistent, and reuse what worked before. Parametric memories need training, consolidation can lose details for good, and keeping every record leaves a growing store to search. We present MIRIX-2.0, a multi-agent memory system designed to be practical, accurate, and efficient at once. It is the most accurate of the compared systems on four of five QA benchmarks. It reaches 91.4% on LoCoMo and 72.6% on LongMemEval-S, where it leads the strongest baseline by 14.3 points, and with AutoDream disabled it gains 31.0 and 22.0 points over HyperMem on single-hop and multi-hop document QA. As procedural memory, it yields the highest mean success…

ai.summary: The paper MIRIX-2.0 presents a multi‑agent memory system that achieves 91.4% on LoCoMo and 72.6% on LongMemEval‑S, outperforming prior systems on four of five QA benchmarks.
ai.why: Developers can use MIRIX-2.0 to give LLM agents persistent, efficient long‑term memory for personalized tasks.

title: AI Reviews Are Biased Towards the Appendix
excerpt: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used by reviewers to highlight weaknesses during the reviewing process, and their outputs often shape the reviews that humans submit. Prior work studies how LLM reviews align with human ones, yet we know little about which parts of a paper these models actually criticize. In this work, we investigate 2,000 papers from ACL, EMNLP, COLM, and ICLR, and show that the latest GPT and Claude models draw about 50% or more of their review weaknesses from the appendix. This behavior holds across the API, coding-agent, and web access methods for using LLMs to review a paper. In contrast, we find that humans draw only 8.4% of their weaknesses from the…

ai.summary: Analysis of 2,000 papers shows that GPT and Claude models generate about 50% of their review weaknesses from the appendix sections, indicating a bias toward that part of documents.
ai.why: Highlights a systematic bias in LLM‑assisted peer review tools, prompting developers to adjust prompting or preprocessing strategies.

title: GH-AWTrace: A Large-Scale Dataset of GitHub Agentic Workflow Execution Logs
excerpt: Agentic workflows enable AI agents to perform recurring repository tasks on schedules or in response to repository events. Existing studies examine workflow definitions and outputs, but provide limited evidence of what happens during execution. We present GH-AWTrace, a dataset linking 25,014 verified GitHub Agentic Workflows across 5,051 repositories to 4,112,526 run records and 562,877 nonempty execution log archives. The dataset preserves execution evidence subject to GitHub's log-retention limits and links it to repository metadata and generated workflow configurations. Illustrative cases show how the logs expose tool denials, provider failures, changes in an agent's approach, and…

ai.summary: GH‑AWTrace releases a dataset of 25,014 verified GitHub Agentic Workflows across 5,051 repositories, including 4,112,526 run records and 562,877 execution logs, to study agentic workflow execution.
ai.why: Provides developers and researchers with real‑world logs to build, evaluate, and improve AI agents that automate repository tasks.

title: DySENSE: Dynamic Spatiotemporal ENergy Synthesis and Emulation with Satellite Imagery
excerpt: Cities account for over two-thirds of the world's energy and more than 70% of global carbon dioxide emissions. City energy is essential for achieving the 2050 net-zero target and the UN's Sustainable Development Goals 7 and 11. Although existing studies have made progress, they are limited by data and methodological gaps. Existing studies are largely predictive for existing cities rather than generative for future cities; fine-grained, aligned monthly dynamic energy data are scarce; and existing GenAI models struggle to generate dynamic urban functional monthly energy. We present DySENSE, a joint multimodal GenAI framework that synthesizes static urban satellite imagery together with…

ai.summary: DySENSE introduces a dynamic spatiotemporal energy synthesis framework that uses satellite imagery to generate fine‑grained, monthly city‑level energy consumption data, addressing gaps in existing predictive models.
ai.why: Researchers and planners can use the synthetic data to model future urban energy scenarios and support net‑zero targets.

title: JVT: Just Video Transformer makes pixel-space video diffusion simple
excerpt: Direct diffusion modeling of high-dimensional raw video data is challenging, and existing pixel-space methods often rely on specialized architectures. We introduce JVT (Just Video Transformer), a simple large-patch DiT-style Transformer for pixel-space video diffusion, without a pretrained autoencoder, auxiliary detailers, cascaded stages, or U-Net-style skip connections. We systematically examine video patch embeddings, register tokens, and adaptive layer normalization to identify design choices that balance generation quality and computational efficiency. The resulting JVT design achieves generation quality competitive with latent diffusion baselines in both class-conditioned and…

ai.summary: JVT (Just Video Transformer) is a large‑patch DiT‑style transformer that performs pixel‑space video diffusion without autoencoders, detailers, or U‑Net skips, simplifying high‑resolution video generation.
ai.why: It offers a simpler architecture for developers building video generation models, potentially reducing engineering overhead.

title: CANTraj: Recovering Vehicle Trajectories from CAN Signals in Naturalistic Driving
excerpt: Open driving releases and usage-based insurance programs often claim to prevent privacy breaches by omitting GPS records when sharing or collecting vehicle data. However, removing GPS coordinates from driving logs does not erase the location information carried by vehicle signals. While prior route-inference attacks have demonstrated that speed, steering, and driving events can be matched to road networks to reconstruct trajectories, existing studies rely on inconsistent prior assumptions and evaluation metrics and are tested only on small, restricted datasets, making their results difficult to compare and their real-world effectiveness uncertain. We release CANTraj, a naturalistic driving…

ai.summary: The paper "CANTraj" demonstrates that vehicle trajectories can be reconstructed from CAN bus signals even when GPS data is removed, exposing privacy risks in naturalistic driving datasets.
ai.why: Developers of telematics and insurance platforms need to consider stronger anonymization methods.

title: MMFlash: Faster Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models
excerpt: Speculative decoding accelerates generation by letting a lightweight drafter propose tokens for parallel verification by a target model. Diffusion drafters such as DFlash propose an entire token block in a single forward pass, but mainly focus on text-only tasks, leaving multimodal drafting underexplored. To study this setting, we first introduce a metric of token-level visual dependence based on the KL divergence between next-token distributions with and without visual input. We find that acceptance rates decrease from 46% in the lowest visual-dependence quartile to 22% in the highest, with this disparity persisting after multimodal training. Motivated by this observation, we propose…

ai.summary: MMFlash proposes a speculative decoding technique for vision‑language models that uses a diffusion drafter to generate token blocks, introducing a token‑level visual dependence metric to evaluate multimodal drafting efficiency.
ai.why: The method can speed up multimodal generation, making real‑time V‑L applications more feasible for developers.

title: Rethinking in Spikes: Mitigating Hallucinations in MDLMs with Step-Aware Decoding
excerpt: Recent advancements in multimodal diffusion language models (MDLMs) have exhibited strong global modeling capabilities through iterative refinement. We observe that mask uncertainty follows an overall downward trend during iterative denoising, while a few denoising steps exhibit localized entropy spikes closely associated with hallucinations. We argue that anomalous steps can be identified by measuring the entropy deviation of each denoising step from its neighboring temporal window. We hypothesize that discrete token commitment discards the distributional information at masked positions, limiting the continued interaction between candidate semantics and the context during entropy spikes…

ai.summary: The paper proposes step‑aware decoding for multimodal diffusion language models, detecting entropy spikes in denoising steps that correlate with hallucinations and adjusting decoding to mitigate them.
ai.why: Offers a practical technique to reduce hallucinations in MDLMs, which developers can integrate into generation pipelines.

title: Loopback Transformer: Towards a Unified View of Residual Looped Transformers
excerpt: Looped Transformers reduce parameter count by repeatedly applying shared blocks, but parameter sharing alone does not determine how the results of repeated computation are reused. We take the depth-memory view of residual connections and analyze which representation is stored after each block application and how later reads weight it. A full block output contains both its input and its new update, so weighting that output also reweights the history already carried by the input. Reading individual updates instead, with the shared stack's input kept on a separate path, gives separate controls over input strength, total update weight, and allocation across updates. The Loopback Transformer…

ai.summary: The Loopback Transformer paper analyzes how residual connections in repeatedly applied shared transformer blocks store and reuse representations, showing that weighting a block’s full output reweights both new updates and the historical input.
ai.why: Provides insights for designing more parameter‑efficient transformer architectures that reuse computation, useful for developers building large models on limited hardware.

title: MEM-SQL: Memory-Empowered Text-to-SQL
excerpt: Text-to-SQL systems translate natural language questions into SQL queries over increasingly complex databases. However, widely used benchmarks evaluate questions independently, overlooking settings where earlier queries over the same database can supply joins or calculations for a new question. We introduce HARE (History-AwaRe Text-to-SQL BEnchmark) to measure the accuracy and cost of adapting historical SQL. HARE comprises 1,600 requests derived from a fixed pool of 823 verified queries across four datasets. Annotations record which components each request preserves and which edits it requires, distinguishing whole-query adaptation from partial reuse. Our method, MEM-SQL (Memory-EMpowered…

ai.summary: MEM-SQL introduces the HARE benchmark, containing 1,600 multi‑turn text‑to‑SQL requests derived from 823 verified queries, to evaluate how systems leverage historical SQL queries for new questions over the same database.
ai.why: Encourages development of text‑to‑SQL models that can maintain context across sessions, improving real‑world database assistants.

title: Mobile AI Factory: Building Specialized Language Models for Your Mobile Device
excerpt: Small language models (SLMs) running on mobile devices can keep user data private and work without connectivity. But they perform well only when fine-tuned for the target task and sized for the target device, a process that today requires repeated expert tuning. We present {\it Mobile AI Factory}, an agentic system that builds a fine-tuned, quantized SLM for a given task and phone. Given a task specification and a target phone, an orchestrator LLM chooses whether to tune hyperparameters, mine real data, or generate synthetic examples, while fixed rules roll back changes that hurt accuracy. The factory searches from small to large models across base models and quantizations, adapts its…

ai.summary: Mobile AI Factory is an agentic system that automatically builds a fine‑tuned, quantized small language model for a specified task and phone model, selecting hyperparameters and data sources via an orchestrator LLM.
ai.why: It enables developers to deploy privacy‑preserving, offline language models on specific devices without manual tuning.

title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
excerpt: Foundation models trained on large unlabeled corpora develop emergent capabilities, tasks that go beyond the training objective. We extend this paradigm to multimodal biology with Bonbon, a foundation model for molecular interactions trained on approximately 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences. From a single representation space, Bonbon exhibits three zero-shot emergent capabilities at hierarchical levels of resolution: functional (mechanism of action), residue (binding site localization, including orthosteric/allosteric discrimination), and bond (covalent versus non-covalent engagement). All three capabilities generalize to out-of-distribution complexes. Bonbon was…

ai.summary: Bonbon is a foundation model trained on ~3.2 trillion protein‑ligand token pairs that, from a single representation space, can zero‑shot predict functional mechanisms, binding residues, and ligand structures.
ai.why: Enables developers to leverage a single model for multiple molecular interaction tasks without task‑specific fine‑tuning, accelerating drug discovery pipelines.

Moreover, existing benchmarks do not meaningfully evaluate whether agents can understand and use audio and video content embedded within web tasks. title: Aligning AI Teams
excerpt: Previous work has shown that alignment training on individual LLM agents can fail to transfer to multi-agent settings. We investigate the underlying mechanisms for this failure, and explore interventions to preserve alignment transfer to multi-agent LLM teams. We focus on two software-engineering tasks (sepsis triage, a news recommender) and ten consulting-proposal generation tasks. We present four findings: (1) The single-vs-team safety gap does not show a clear trend with more capable models. We find that Anthropic's Mythos Preview shows the largest gap on one of our tasks but the smallest on another; (2) Many natural interventions, such as having agents critique each other's work or…

ai.summary: The paper studies why alignment training on single LLM agents does not transfer to multi‑agent teams, using sepsis triage, news recommendation, and consulting‑proposal tasks, and identifies four key findings about safety gaps and model capabilities.

title: HALO: Human-Aligned Data Collection for WhoLe-body MObile Manipulation
excerpt: Learning whole-body mobile manipulation requires demonstrations that coordinate bimanual actions with locomotion across extended workspaces. However, existing interfaces trade off direct robot control, perception and action alignment, and natural operator mobility, making such demonstrations difficult to collect. We introduce HALO, a human-aligned data collection system for whole-body mobile manipulation. The system aligns the operator's perception and action space with the robot while preserving direct physical feedback and natural locomotion. Operators guide the robot end-effectors through kinesthetic teaching and move a low-resistance platform without the deployed mobile base while…

ai.summary: HALO is a data‑collection system that aligns a human operator’s perception and action space with a whole‑body mobile robot, enabling bimanual manipulation combined with locomotion while preserving natural mobility.

title: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent
excerpt: We introduce Gamer, a generalist agent framework built for long-horizon tasks in complex interactive environments. We first continue pre-training on a dataset constructed from tens of thousands of hours of device-level keyboard and mouse interaction. These trajectories span simulated games and embodied environments, allowing the model to learn environmental dynamics across both physical and virtual domains. Sparse-thinking instruction tuning then…

title: VibePrevisBench: Evaluating Agentic Coding for 4D Scene Generation in Blender
excerpt: Controllable real-world video generation models can condition on a rendered graybox proxy video, which fixes layout, motion and camera. Coding agents can build such videos by reconstructing a 4D scene in Blender, yet no benchmark checks both these videos and the long, multi-shot scenes behind them. We introduce VibePrevisBench, a benchmark for 4D scene reconstruction: an agent turns a brief into an executable 4D scene and renders its proxy video. Its 242 tasks span four input kinds, including scripts, photos, continuations, and reference videos. Each delivery is scored along two evaluation dimensions. Rule-based Scene Check re-runs the code and compares the exported 4D scene with hidden…

ai.summary: VibePrevisBench is a new benchmark that evaluates coding agents on 242 tasks requiring them to reconstruct 4D scenes in Blender from briefs and render proxy videos, testing both scene generation and multi‑shot video quality.

title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
excerpt: The release of GPT-6 Astra marks the emergence of a new paradigm in robotics: agentic robotics. Within weeks, frontier models with agentic harnesses matched or exceeded task-specific policies on many embodied benchmarks. Instead of training a dedicated policy for each family of tasks, an agentic robotic system applies a foundation model to open-world embodied tasks. It operates in a closed loop: observing the environment, interpreting user intent, reasoning about the task, invoking skills and tools, verifying outcomes, and adapting its strategy. Despite these advances, the community has yet to converge on a shared definition, a reliable evaluation framework, or a research roadmap. We argue…

title: V-JEPA-LM: Video-Language Models That Read Dynamics Beyond Static, Text-Aligned Representations
excerpt: World-model video encoders such as V-JEPA learn how scenes change (direction, speed, order, state) from video alone. To answer questions, they are joined to a language model trained on captions and question-answer pairs. But each caption or question names only a few attributes of a clip, so the model learns to retrieve those attributes rather than to read the clip, and the dynamics the encoder carries go unused: on the same items, a linear probe reads speed from frozen V-JEPA features at 87% while the VLM answers at chance. We show where dynamics lives in a frozen encoder: in a subspace shared across videos for predictive encoders such as V-JEPA, but not as a shared component of frame-wise…

ai.summary: V-JEPA-LM combines a video-world-model encoder (V-JEPA) that learns scene dynamics from raw video with a language model trained on captions and QA pairs, but the language side only uses a few attributes per clip, leaving most dynamic features unused; a linear probe can read speed from frozen V-JEPA features with 87% accuracy.
ai.why: Shows that video encoders capture rich dynamics that can be exploited for downstream tasks beyond captioning, suggesting new ways to build video‑language systems.

title: G-CAST: Governed Continual Self-Training for E-Commerce Agents under Evolving Demands
